questions.question: The formula for average gradient is:
A gradient of 1 : 5 means:
options: The land rises 5 m for every 1 m travelled horizontally
The land rises 1 m for every 5 m travelled horizontally

questions.question: Which slope is STEEPER?

subtopics.title: Extracting VI and HE from the Map

questions.question: The vertical interval between trig beacon 251 (1 200 m) and the spot height (900 m) is:
Two points measure 9 cm apart on a 1:50 000 map. The real horizontal distance is:
Why must the horizontal equivalent of 4,5 km be converted to 4 500 m before dividing?
options: Because kilometres are not allowed in geography
Because the VI and HE must be in the same units for the ratio to have meaning
Because the memo prefers big numbers

questions.question: Which two map symbols provided the exact heights for this calculation?
options: A bench mark and a river
A trig beacon and a spot height

subtopics.title: The Calculation — Laid Out for Marks

questions.question: Simplifying 300 m ÷ 4 500 m to the form 1 : x gives:
Why does an answer left as '300/4 500' or '0,067' typically lose the final mark?
options: The memo requires the answer in the ratio form 1 : x

questions.question: The correct interpretation of 1 : 15 is:
options: The land rises 1 m vertically for every 15 m travelled horizontally
The land rises 15 m for every 1 m travelled

questions.question: Why is the answer called an AVERAGE gradient?
options: Because it is calculated from average heights
Because the real land may dip and climb between the points; the ratio smears the total rise evenly over the total distance
Because several learners' answers are averaged
Because the map scale is approximate

subtopics.title: Verification, Traps and the Full Method

questions.question: A learner divides 300 m by 4,5 and reports 1 : 66,7. What went wrong?
options: Mixed units: the 4,5 was kilometres and should have been converted to 4 500 m

questions.question: A learner reports the answer as 15 : 1. What error is this?
options: An inverted ratio — the vertical '1 metre of climb' must lead the ratio
It is equivalent and equally correct

questions.question: Which quick reverse-check confirms the simplification 1 : 15?
Why does a 2 mm measuring error matter on a 1:50 000 map?
options: It represents 100 m of real ground, distorting the HE and the final ratio
It does not matter at all

questions.question: The stairs and the parking ramp both reach the same floor. What makes the ramp gentler?
options: It lifts you a smaller height
You travel much further along for the same height gained

questions.question: The sugar-in-the-jug picture — one spoon in a cup tastes sweeter than one spoon in a two-litre jug — explains why:
options: 1 : 150 is gentler than 1 : 15, because the same 1 m of climb is spread over more walking
Gradients must always be written as decimals

questions.question: In the plain-language version, the 'up' number and the 'along' number are properly called:
options: The vertical interval and the horizontal equivalent

questions.question: A slope written as 1 : 20 is saying:
options: You walk 20 m along for every 1 m you climb
You climb 20 m for every 1 m you walk
The slope rises 20% of the time

subtopics.title: Two Numbers Off the Map, Both Speaking Metres

questions.question: A small triangle printed with a station number and a height beside it is:
options: A trig beacon, a surveyed point whose height is exact
A bench mark on a road

questions.question: Beacon 251 stands at 1 200 m and the spot height at 900 m. The 'up' number is found by:
options: Taking the lower from the higher: 300 m

questions.question: Dividing 300 m by 4,5 km is compared in the lesson to:
options: Working out a price by dividing rands by cents — the answer is out by a thousand and means nothing
Buying airtime with a bank card

questions.question: Measuring 9 cm between the two points on a 1:50 000 sheet gives the 'along' number as:
options: 4 500 m, after multiplying by 50 000 and stepping down from centimetres

subtopics.title: Share It Out, Then Say It in One Line

questions.question: Sharing 4 500 m of walking among 300 m of climbing is like asking:
options: How many R300 vouchers R4 500 buys — the answer is 15
How much R4 500 grows in a year
How many metres are in a kilometre
How steep a staircase is in degrees

questions.question: Handing in '0,067' instead of '1 : 15' is compared in the lesson to:
options: Handing over a fifty-rand note torn in half — the value is there but nobody will take it

questions.question: Which sentence correctly explains what 1 : 15 feels like on the ground?
options: It is nearly flat — a railway would run on it easily
It rises 15 m for every metre walked, so it is a cliff
It rises 1 m for every 15 m travelled — properly steep, and gentler than about 1 : 50 is what a railway needs
It cannot be walked at all

questions.question: If subtracting the heights the wrong way round gives you a negative number, you should:
options: Take the size of the difference — steepness does not depend on which point you stand at
